description: Fruit Slice online free: juicy fruit flies up from the board — swipe to slice it. Three lives, double points for combos, and bombs to avoid.
lede: The juiciest arcade game in your browser. Watermelons, oranges, apples and kiwis fly up from the cutting board, and your finger is the blade. Swipe through them to slice them in half — three or more in one stroke is a combo worth double points. But watch out: miss a fruit and you lose a life, and one touch of a bomb costs a life too. You have three lives, so make every swipe count.

p: Press Start slicing and the fruit starts flying up from the bottom of the board. Swipe or drag your finger or mouse across a fruit to slice it in half for 10 points. Fruit arcs up and falls back down under gravity, so a fruit you ignore will fall off the board — and every fruit you miss costs you one of your three lives — except during the first ten seconds, a warm-up where missed fruit costs nothing, so you can learn the swipe first.

Bombs fly up mixed in with the fruit. They are black, round, and sparking — never swipe through one. Touching a bomb costs a life too. When all three lives are gone, you see your score, how many fruits you sliced, and your best combo.

Every fruit is worth 10 points on its own. Slice three or more fruits in a single swipe and each one is worth 20 instead — that is how big scores happen. A long swipe across a cluster of fruit is worth far more than three careful little cuts.

You start with three lives. A fruit that falls off the board unsliced costs one life, and so does a bomb you slice by mistake. Bombs that fall off the board on their own cost nothing, so when in doubt, let a bomb fall.

sections.h: From arcade cabinets to the touchscreen
p: Slicing fruit with a blade became a gaming craze in 2010, when Fruit Ninja launched on phones and turned a simple idea — swipe to slice — into one of the most downloaded mobile games ever made. Its secret was the feeling: fruit bursting into halves with a spray of juice is satisfying in a way a button press never is.

The idea has been copied in countless slicing games since, because it needs no tutorial at all: anyone who has ever cut an apple understands it at once. The version here keeps that same one-gesture rule, adds combos for slicing several fruits in a single swipe, and keeps the bombs as the one thing you must never touch.

ol: Wait for clusters. Fruit spawns in waves, and a swipe through three fruits at once is worth double per fruit — patience pays more than fast little cuts.
Swipe across the arc, not at the fruit. A long diagonal stroke through the middle of the screen catches fruit at different heights in one motion.
Let bombs fall. A bomb that drops off the board costs you nothing, so never chase a fruit that has a bomb right next to it.
Slice near the top of the arc. Fruit slows down at the top of its flight, so it hangs there for a moment — the easiest moment to catch two or three at once.
On a phone, hold the device in one hand and swipe with a finger of the other. Short flicks are faster and more accurate than long drags.

p: For another fast, one-more-go classic, whack the moles in [[whack-a-mole]]. If you would rather climb than slice, bounce up the sky in [[doodle-jump]]. You can find every fast, one-more-go game in [[cat:arcade|arcade games]].

faq: How do I slice the fruit?
Swipe or drag your finger or mouse across a fruit. The white blade trail shows where your swipe went — anything the trail crosses gets sliced.
How many points is a fruit worth?
10 points on its own. Slice three or more fruits in one swipe and each one is worth 20 points instead.
What happens if I miss a fruit?
It falls off the board and you lose one of your three lives — except during the first ten seconds, a warm-up where missed fruit costs nothing. Bombs that fall off the board never cost a life.
What happens if I slice a bomb?
You lose one life, the screen flashes red, and the round keeps going. Lose all three lives and the round is over.
How many lives do I get?
Three. You lose one for every fruit that falls unsliced and for every bomb you touch.
